html:
Dakeł Keyoh is the land of the Dakelh, or Carrier, an Athabaskan people of the central interior of British Columbia, around Stuart, Fraser and François lakes. A keyoh is a family's hunting and trapping territory, passed down in the clan.

They lived by fishing for salmon in the rivers and lakes and by hunting and trapping. The name Carrier is said to come from an old custom in which a widow carried her husband's ashes for a time. Their western neighbours were the Wet'suwet'en, who speak a related language.

In 1806 Simon Fraser of the North West Company founded Fort St. James on Stuart Lake, later a main post of the Hudson's Bay Company. In 1885 the missionary Adrien-Gabriel Morice made a syllabic script for their language. Today the Dakelh make up many First Nations across the region.
